messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a ~20% p95 decode latency regression on host-proxy canary after the kernel-picker change deployed earlier. Impact shows up for streaming endpoints (http2) with small chunk sizes :eyes:
cheng: Interesting. Which canary, and do you have flamegraphs/pprof?
maya: canary-23. Here's the quick triage: flamegraph (internal link) https://perf.redwood/fg/5860001234 and pprof snapshot attached. Pattern: host-side parse + proto-unpack spikes, then kernel selection path shows a different conv kernel than before.
alex: Possible kernel mismatch due to sequence-length heuristics? If the selector now prefers packing kernels for medium seqs we could be losing in L2 locality for small streaming batches.
taylor: Any KV-cache eviction noise? small streaming requests often bypass prefix cache and then re-warm which can amplify host parse costs.
maya: KV hot-shard evictions correlate. I ran a 1-hour trace and saw repeated kv.get for the same key with 10-20ms gaps. p95 host parse up 12ms on average. Perf sample snippet:
```
# perf top-ish flame excerpt (simplified)
parse_stream+0x1f4  18%
proto_unwrap+0x90 12%
kernel_selector_choose+0x3b 9%
kv_cache_miss_handle+0x58 8%
net_http2_decode_frame+0x2a 7%
```
cheng: That kernel_selector line is suspect. Did we change any fallback rules? I recall PR #492 changed threshold from 64->96 tokens for packed kernels.
maya: Yup, PR #492. Reversing threshold locally reduces p95 back to baseline in sandbox. Repro steps (quick):
```bash
# quick repro against canary image
curl -v --http2 -N -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input":"short prompts","stream":true}' https://canary-23.internal.redwood/v1/stream
# run for 30s with 50rps small chunks (8-32 bytes)
```
alex: So two amplifiers: (1) selector picks a kernel with worse host-prep locality for these small frames, (2) KV miss churn exposes the parse penalty repeatedly.
taylor: Also check grpc/http2 small-frame handling — we changed coalescing in the proxy recently (PR #508). Could be smaller writev/flush patterns leading to more parse work.
maya: Confirmed: turning off proxy micro-coalesce decreases host parse syscalls by ~35%.
perf-bot: [automated] created perf-issue #2023 linking traces and comparison diffs.
cheng: Plan: 1) revert selector threshold on canary and measure 24h, 2) add protective heuristic: if http2 small-chunk high-rate, prefer low-overhead kernel even if less compute-efficient, 3) add kv-cache pin for frequent streaming sessions.
alex: I'll own (2). Will add a rate-aware override where if avg chunk < 64B and RPS > 20, force the slim kernel path. Patch target branch: runtime/kernel-selector.
taylor: I'll validate proxy coalesce params and post a canary with adjusted writev policy.
maya: I'll run a focused A/B on canary-23 with reverted selector threshold + proxy tweak and collect p50/p95/cpu. Posting telemetry in ~2h.
cheng: Thanks. If this looks good we can roll a fastfix and then follow up with a proper kernel-cost model to avoid heuristics drift.
maya: +1, thanks all. :thumbsup:
